description: Create or update a defect — a tracked problem found by testing. Without `id` it creates, with `id` it updates. Creating one requires `title`, `actual_result` and `severity`; the API rejects a defect missing any of the three. Severity is given as a label ("blocker", "critical", "major", "normal", "minor", "trivial") and the server maps it to the workspace's numeric ID, custom options included. Status is a label too ("open", "in_progress", "resolved", "invalid") and passes through as written; setting it to "resolved" on an existing defect goes through the dedicated resolve endpoint. When the defect comes from a specific test failure, use qase_triage_defect instead. The API has no way to attach runs or results to a defect, so reference the failing results in the text rather than expecting a link. Find existing defects with qql_search before filing a duplicate. Cost: one API call, about 0.5s, plus a cached lookup of the severity options.

actual_result.description: What actually happened — required when creating a defect

code.description: Project code (2-10 uppercase letters, numbers, or underscores)

custom_field.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID, e.g. { "12": "value" }

id.description: Defect ID — if provided, updates; if omitted, creates

severity.description: How bad the defect is — required when creating a defect

status.description: Set to "resolved" to resolve the defect

name: qase_defect_upsert
title: Create or update defect
